data.title: Folding Bikes Were Never Built for Everyone? DAHON is Fixing That
data.description:
SACRAMENTO, Calif., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- For over forty years, DAHON has offered freedom that fits more riders. Behind that mission is Founder and CEO Dr. David Hon, whose entrepreneurial journey began in laser research.

DAHON's ultra-light folding e-bike K-Feather made a splash when it was launched. Now the company's new Heavy Duty Folding Bike Series – Mariner XL and Mariner HD – are probably the first folding bikes built specifically for heavier riders, rated to offer 150 kg (330 lb) payload, roughly 40% higher than typical folding bikes.

The Road Not Taken – Physicist Turned Entrepreneur

A physicist at Hughes Research Laboratories, Dr. Hon was inspired by the 1970s oil crisis to pursue greener urban transport. "Initially, I wanted to license my patents, but no factory was willing to produce them. So, I raised funds on my own, built a factory to manufacture and market them," said Dr. Hon.

The first DAHON folding bicycle appeared in 1982, pioneering modern folding bicycle design and earning Dr. Hon recognition as the "Father of the Modern Folding Bicycle."

Dr. Hon had taken the road less travelled by. More than four decades on, and that has made all the difference.

Frame Flex Is Costing Riders Watts – DAHON Fixes That

Dr. Hon's scientific approach lives on in DAHON-V Tech, combining physics, computerized finite element analysis and strain gauges to evaluate bicycle stiffness.

DAHON's DELTECH cable and Super Down Tube can increase frame stiffness by 33% and riding speed by 5–15%, according to DAHON's internal testing. Results vary with test conditions and bicycle configuration.

Folding Bikes for All Riders, Aspirations Unchanged

From the approximately 12 kg K-Feather electric-assist folder to the Heavy Duty Series, DAHON is widening access to cycling. Its independent sub-brand BICECO targets the mass market.

Looking ahead, DAHON plans to advance DAHON-V Tech, expand its tri-fold carbon frame series and electric-assist ranges, and pursue targeted acquisitions in new materials and core technologies.

From solving the portability problem in 1982 to widening its international footprint today, the ambition has not changed: make cycling a practical, everyday choice.

About DAHON

Founded in California in 1982 by Dr. David T. Hon, DAHON is a global folding bicycle brand and pioneer of modern folding bikes. DAHON TECH is listed on HKEX (2543).

data.title: Cebu Pacific Named Most Reliable Philippine Carrier in TIME's 2027 Rankings
data.description:
MANILA, Philippines, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cebu Pacific () ranked as the top Philippine carrier and second in Southeast Asia on TIME's 2027 Most Reliable Airlines list.

Developed with global data firm Statista, TIME's Most Reliable Airlines ranking assessed more than 30 million flights worldwide from July 2025 to June 2026. Using independent data from aviation analytics firm OAG, the assessment measured reliability based on punctuality and cancellation rates. Participating airlines also had to meet passenger volume and data coverage requirements and pass a safety screening.

"Becoming the most reliable Philippine carrier starts with our people. It takes the collective commitment, expertise and dedication of our teams across every part of the operation – from our flight and cabin crews to engineering, ground operations and our operations control center. By investing in our people, strengthening our processes, leveraging technology and operating a modern and well-maintained fleet, we continue to build a culture of operational excellence. Together, these efforts enable us to deliver a safe, efficient and reliable travel experience for our passengers every time they fly with us," said Javier Massot, CEB Chief Operations Officer.

The TIME ranking follows another independent assessment of CEB's operational performance. In April 2026, CEB was the most punctual Philippine carrier and ranked fifth among Asia-Pacific airlines, with an 84.98% on-time arrival rate across more than 12,000 systemwide flights, based on data from aviation analytics firm Cirium.

Behind these results are sustained investments in people, training, technology and fleet modernization. In April 2026, CEB opened the Cebu Pacific Training Academy in Parañaque City. The 1,685-square-meter facility features Airbus A330 and ATR door trainers, cabin mock-ups and slide trainers, and provides hands-on training for pilots and cabin crew.

The airline also upgraded its Network Control Center (NCC) into the CEB Operations Control Center (OCC), adopting a more integrated, digital-first approach to monitoring flights, managing disruptions and coordinating operational decisions.

CEB continues to build a more modern fleet as it works toward operating an all-NEO jet fleet by 2030. Beginning in 2027, the airline will also introduce Starlink, enhancing the passenger experience and improving operational connectivity for its flight crews and operational teams.

CEB currently flies to 34 domestic and 24 international destinations across Asia, Australia and the Middle East.

data.title: Sunjay Kapur Family Trust Dispute Back in SC After Mediation Fails
data.description:
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday closed the mediation proceedings in the inheritance dispute among industrialist Sunjay Kapur's widow Priya, mother Rani and his children over the ownership of the RK Family Trust, after the family members failed to reach any settlement. The SC had in May appointed former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud as the mediator to help resolve the family dispute over the ownership of the trust, which holds a stake in Sona Group flagship Sona BLW Precision Forgings (Sona Comstar).

The mediation has reached an impasse despite 15 sittings, the retired judge said in his latest report, prompting the SC to end the settlement process and proceed with hearing of the dispute. According to the mediator's report, claims of Samaira and Kiaan, Sunjay Kapur's children from ex-wife Karisma Kapoor, can be resolved, but the mediation reached an impasse on Rani's claims.-Indu Bhan

data.title: End to Sponsorship IBM Asks Some US Staff to Shift Abroad or Quit by Dec 31
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Technology major IBM has given some of its US-based employees holding H-1B visas and green cards three weeks to relocate overseas or leave the company, as it moves to end immigration sponsorship for most positions in its consulting division. Employees who decline overseas transfers have been offered three months' severance, with December 31 set as their last working day.

The decision affects IBM Consulting, the company's largest business division, which employs more than 150,000 people globally. IBM has not disclosed the number of employees affected by the move. Some workers were reportedly informed of the decision during individual meetings with managers. India could emerge as the largest destination for employees opting to relocate.

Of the 1,278 consulting vacancies IBM listed outside the US on November 19, 1,125 were in India, compared with 23 in Singapore and 18 in the UK. However, the company has not clarified how many of these openings are meant for employees affected by the decision. The financial implications of relocation could also be significant. An IBM employee, writing anonymously on workplace discussion platform Blind, said "the relocation offer could mean an 80% pay cut for those moving to India, or losing their jobs by December 31." The company announced earlier this month that it would discontinue US visa and green card sponsorship for most positions in its consulting division.

The company said its participation in high-skilled visa programmes had been declining for several years, citing changing skill availability and client requirements. The move comes amid tighter scrutiny of employment-based immigration in the US. In October, the US Department of Labor suspended eight companies from the Permanent Labor Certification programme, a key step towards employment-based green cards. The companies include Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Tech and Capgemini.

data.title: Sunjay Kapur Family Trust Row Back in SC After Mediation Fails
data.description:
Indu Bhan New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday closed the mediation proceedings in the inheritance dispute among industrialist Sunjay Kapur's widow Priya, mother Rani and his children over the ownership of the RK Family Trust, after the family members failed to reach a settlement. The apex court had in May appointed former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud as the mediator to help resolve the family dispute over the ownership of the trust, which holds a stake in Sona Group flagship Sona BLW Precision Forgings (Sona Comstar).

The mediation reached an impasse despite 15 sittings, the retired judge said in his latest report, prompting the SC to end the settlement process and proceed with the hearing of the dispute. According to the mediator's report, the claims of Samaira and Kiaan, Sunjay Kapur's children from ex-wife Karisma Kapoor, can be resolved, but the mediation reached an impasse over Rani's claims.

While reserving its order on Thursday, a bench led by Justice JB Pardiwala noted that the mediation had concluded without a settlement. While questioning whether Rani Kapur would gain anything at the end of the litigation considering her age of 81, the court asked her senior counsel, Siddharth Dave, what exactly she wanted from the trust. Was she seeking a monetary settlement or the entire corpus of the trust, Justice Pardiwala asked.

Dave submitted that Rani Kapur was seeking both money and assets constituting the trust's corpus. While she sought 6,000 crore from the trust to settle the case, Samaira and Kiaan demanded 26.66% of the total trust corpus of around 30,000 crore. The bench reiterated that Rani Kapur should show flexibility and take a practical view of the dispute. Senior counsel Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Priya Kapur, told the court that Rani had walked out of the mediation and was now blaming her daughter-in-law for the failure of the settlement process.

He said Priya was willing to pursue an amicable resolution, but sought Rani's personal participation in the mediation process. Priya is entitled to 60%, with the remaining 40% to be shared among Sunjay Kapur's children, the counsel said, adding that the multi-generational trust was meant to pass down through the generations and could not simply be split up like this.

Opposing this submission, Dave alleged that the money and assets of the trust were not being properly managed and that Priya was effectively sitting on the trust's funds and assets. He said Rani had lost both her husband and her son, and meeting her daughter-in-law caused her considerable anxiety. However, she is willing to meet the mediator separately, he said. Sunjay Kapur, former chairman of auto parts company Sona BLW Precision Forgings, died in the UK last year while playing polo. His death triggered power struggle within family over control and inheritance of the Sona Group empire.

data.title: HDFC Bank to Bring Key Digital Apps In-house
data.description:
HDFC Bank, India's second-largest by deposits and assets, is bringing critical digital banking and payment platforms in-house after cyberattacks at financial firms exposed third-party outsourcing risks. Saloni Shukla reports. 13 Saloni Shukla Mumbai: HDFC Bank, India's second-largest by both deposits and assets, is bringing critical digital banking and payment platforms in-house after repeated cyberattacks on fintech companies, NBFCs, and vulnerable application programming interfaces exposed third-party outsourcing risks in the financing industry. "We are bringing our card platforms, including MyCards and OnlyCards, in-house.

We are also in the process of insourcing PayZapp," Ramesh Lakshminarayanan, group head of information technology and chief information officer at HDFC Bank, told ET. "Several third-party applications are being brought in-house," the country's most-valued lender told ET. HDFC Bank aims to eventually develop and maintain 70% of its key applications in-house, particularly mobile banking, net banking and payments platforms.

The bank, which had previously faced regulatory curbs over technology gaps in some customer deliverables, has also shut down BizX, a third-party platform serving small proprietorships, and integrated its functionality into existing systems. It is also strengthening API authentication, certificate management and monitoring of third-party connections to mitigate cybersecurity risks arising from vulnerabilities across the wider banking ecosystem. "Our strategy is to eventually develop and maintain 60-70% of our key applications in-house in the next few years," Lakshminarayanan said. "Critical platforms such as mobile banking, net banking and core payments, API management need to be under our control.

These are the crown jewels, and having our own technology capabilities is essential to securing them and remaining competitive." Third-party risks have consumed boardroom mind space across the financial industry following a spate of cyberattacks in the past three months, with NBFCs losing more than 300 crore and over 150 cyberfraud complaints being lodged across the country.

Risk Mitigation In October alone, around 20 financial institutions were affected by attacks involving stolen partner-bank credentials and vulnerabilities in payment and disbursement APIs, ET had reported. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has since issued multiple advisories, warning of cybercriminals exploiting weaknesses in fintech platforms, payment gateways and third-party technology integrations to initiate unauthorised fund transfers.

In its latest advisory on November 20, the agency said such attacks had spread beyond financial institutions to technology service providers handling government-linked payments and platforms processing vendor and business-partner payouts. Lakshminarayanan said conventional third-party risk management, which relies heavily on periodic audits and security certifications, is becoming inadequate as cyberattacks grow more sophisticated. "Banks have traditionally relied on third-party risk management teams to conduct periodic audits and obtain security certifications from vendors.

But that is no longer sufficient. We now need to understand, in real time, what is happening across the systems of third-party entities connected to us," he said. HDFC Bank is consequently tightening authentication requirements for third-party connections, strengthening certificate management and reviewing API access controls. "We are introducing stronger controls around how APIs are accessed and transactions are authorised.

Even when a third party is integrated with the bank, there needs to be greater assurance that the transaction has been initiated by an authorised person. We are also strengthening certificate management and other API security controls," Lakshminarayanan said. The bank's insourcing strategy is also intended to give its technology teams greater visibility and control over software development and security.

data.title: Centre Reminds Netflix to Block Pakistani Shows
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: The ministry of information and broadcasting (MIB) has asked Netflix to ensure Pakistani-origin content is not made available to viewers in India amid complaints over possible release of Pakistani web series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo in the country. The ministry has told the streaming platform to continue complying with its May 8, 2025, advisory and maintain its previously communicated position of not making Pakistani-origin films and series available in India, people aware of the development said.

The development follows opposition from the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA), which urged the government to stop the series from streaming in India. In a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the association also called for a permanent law banning Pakistani films, web series, songs, podcasts and other content on Indian platforms. Netflix has not publicly commented. Industry insiders said the platform is treating the series as a global release rather than a territory-specific launch, with the project believed to have been greenlit by its Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) team.

Issued on May 8, 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack, the MIB advisory asked OTT platforms, streaming services and intermediaries operating in India to discontinue Pakistani-origin web series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming content, whether subscription-based or otherwise, citing national security concerns. Legal experts said the advisory is not necessarily a blanket statutory ban, though OTT platforms may avoid risking friction with the government.

Pakistani entertainment continues to reach Indian audiences through digital platforms. Dramas such as Dar-e-Nijaat (Door to Salvation) are accessed through YouTube channels and the ARY Plus app, though their official availability in India could not be independently verified. Veto, a subscription-free streaming platform operated by Veto Streaming Media, recently streamed the Pakistan-England-Sri Lanka tri-series held in Pakistan.

Its directors include India TV promoters Rajat Sharma and Ritu Dhawan. Following the May 2025 advisory, FanCode stopped streaming the remaining matches of Pakistan Super League T20 cricket tournament, while Sony Sports Network halted its scheduled television coverage. Zee Entertainment Enterprises removed Pakistani programming from ZEE5 and its Zee Zindagi YouTube channel. Based on Farhat Ishtiaq's bestselling novel and directed by Momina Duraid, Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo Part 1 premieres globally on Netflix on December 4. Its availability in India remains unclear. Separately, two private screenings of Pakistani drama Dar-e-Nijaat, which has gained traction among Indian viewers on social media, were cancelled in Bengaluru following online backlash and police scrutiny, highlighting the continuing debate over access to Pakistani entertainment in India.

data.title: Private Fuel Retailers Post Sales Drop in Oct, State OMCs Gain
data.description:
Reliance-BP, Nayara hiked pump prices by 3-5/litre Sanjeev Choudhary New Delhi: Private fuel retailers, led by Reliance-BP and Nayara Energy, recorded a 44% year-on-year decline in diesel sales and 16% in petrol in October, as comparatively higher prices pushed customers towards state-run rivals. The shift boosted diesel and petrol sales at state-run retailers, including Indian Oil (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum (HPCL), by 20% and 6%, respectively, according to official data.

A surge in international crude and fuel prices prompted private retailers to raise pump rates by 3-5 per litre in October. State-run companies, however, abstained from any increase. The resulting price gap drove customers away from private pumps, particularly commercial buyers, for whom even small price differences can translate into substantial savings due to large volumes.

Before raising prices, private retailers had also capped the volume of diesel customers could buy at their pumps, prompting a warning from the oil ministry. State-run companies' retail pumps are also absorbing additional demand from bulk customers, who accounted for about 13% of India's diesel sales in 2025-26. With bulk diesel, which is typically sold at a discount to retail, now about 40 per litre pricier, some large consumers moved purchases to petrol pumps.

This contributed to a 33% year-on-year drop in bulk diesel sales in October. State-run retailers are managing the additional demand from both these shifts smoothly, unlike in the first few months of the Iran war, when a sudden surge in demand led to reports of brief shortages in some states. Having learnt from that experience, they can now anticipate the additional demand and ensure adequate supplies at individual stations, said an industry executive.

data.title: HMSI to Focus on Dealer Margins, Buyer Retention
data.description:
in a shift away from pursuing market share... Shally Seth Mohile Mumbai: Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI) is prioritising dealer profitability and customer retention over pushing market share in the country's fiercely competitive two-wheeler market, with greater focus on expanding its vehicles in operation than chasing annual volume rankings. "Share is just one year's result.

Our business is not just one year," HMSI president and chief executive Tsutsumu Otani told ET. HMSI has been the country's second-largest two-wheeler maker since its separation from Hero MotoCorp in 2014, and even outsold its former partner in monthly sales on multiple occasions. During April-October FY27, HMSI's domestic dispatches stood at 3.7 million units, while Hero MotoCorp dispatched 4.0 million units.

Otani said HMSI will focus on growing and maintaining its units in operation (UIO), or the number of Honda vehicles on Indian roads. "For the dealer network, the most important thing is units in operation, not share," he said. "Honda tries to maintain units in operation. That means maintaining and protecting our dealer network, profitability and business." The strategy marks a shift in emphasis from the pursuit of market leadership to building a sustainable customer base in a market where competition has intensified across commuter motorcycles, scooters and premium bikes.

The focus on customer retention and repeat purchases comes as HMSI looks to tap growth across segments. The company sees considerable headroom in the motorcycle market, which Otani estimates at 23-24 million units annually. He also sees greater participation of women in personal mobility as an opportunity to expand the scooter market. Women currently account for only 10% of HMSI's business. A change in this mix could open up a new avenue of growth for the company, Otani said. HMSI registrations have been averaging 10-15% growth over the previous year, he said. The company expects sales during the September-November festive period to exceed 1.9 million units, compared with over 1.8 million units in the corresponding period last year.

data.title: D-St Shrugs Off Tariff Fears for Now, Select Stocks to Lead Play
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: Indian equities rose on Thursday, tracking gains across Asian markets, as investors took the proposed 25% US tariffs in their stride amid expectations that their impact could be less damaging than initially feared. However, benchmark indices pared a part of their intraday gains to end the session higher. The Sensex and Nifty had gained around 0.7% during the session before trimming gains toward the close.

The NSE Nifty 50 advanced 0.3% to 25,884.5, its highest closing level since February 11, while the BSE Sensex rose 0.5% to 84,328.6, its strongest close since January 7. Both indices are now about 1% away from erasing their losses for the year. The gains came despite the US proposing 25% tariffs on India on November 25. A trade deal could bring the proposed rate down to 17%, according to information available to investors.

The proposal is yet to come into force, limiting its potential near-term impact on markets. The impact on individual exporters will depend on the products covered and their ability to redirect shipments. A 17% tariff under a trade deal could give India a 1-3 percentage-point advantage over some emerging-market peers, Jefferies said in its latest note. Sunny Agrawal of SBI Capital Markets said tariff-related concerns were largely concentrated in home textile and shrimp companies, as well as businesses with significant exposure to the US market.

He said pharmaceuticals and semiconductors were among the sectors unlikely to be covered by the proposed tariffs. "The hit is predominantly on textile and shrimp-related businesses and individual companies where US business exposure is very high," he said. Agrawal said there was scope for negotiations, with the final tariff rate likely to be either 17% or 25%.

He added that India's tariff position relative to competing export-oriented economies such as China, Bangladesh and Pakistan would be important, noting that the country could have a 1-2 percentage-point advantage over some peers.Thursday's gains extended a sharp rally in November, which has lifted the Nifty more than 12%. Record foreign inflows of about $15 billion this month have further supported the momentum, placing India among the best-performing major equity markets globally.

Agrawal said benchmark indices could enter a consolidation phase after their recent gains, with market leadership shifting towards select sectors and stocks. He said the rally had largely been driven by 15-20 heavyweight companies and could continue if foreign institutional investor flows remained positive, alongside buying interest in large companies such as Reliance Industries and TCS. "Going forward, even frontline indices may get into a consolidation mode, and sector rotation may begin," he said, adding that selective opportunities could emerge in segments outside the Nifty, including real estate and small-cap stocks.

He also expects some consolidation in banking stocks until the RBI policy announcement. Sector and market-cap rotation could remain a feature of the market over the next one to two months, potentially extending until the Union Budget, he said. Meanwhile, a 6% rise in Brent crude over the previous two sessions amid continued hostilities in the Middle East kept investors cautious. Technology-heavy Asian markets advanced as risk appetite improved. HDFC Bank was the biggest contributor to the Nifty's gains, rising 2.4%. The Nifty IT index emerged as the best-performing sectoral gauge, climbing 3.5%, while the Nifty FMCG index was the biggest laggard. Overall, eight of the 15 sectoral indices on the NSE ended lower.

data.title: Piramal Pharma's in Good Health with Rich Biz Mix
data.description:
Snehal Mergu ET Intelligence Group: Piramal Pharma's growth momentum is expected to strengthen, driven by rising traction in the CDMO (contract development and manufacturing organisation) business, growing pipeline of late-stage molecules, and increasing contribution from high-value innovation and on-patent manufacturing. Improving utilisation and richer business mix are expected to support margin expansion.

After strong performance in the September 2026 quarter with consolidated revenue rising 28% and Ebitda soaring 72% year-on-year, the company has upgraded the FY27 revenue growth guidance to 19-20% from low-to-mid-teens and expects profits to grow even faster, with second half of the year likely to be stronger than the first half. Its shares have gained 21% in a month.

Analysts have maintained a 'Buy' rating on the stock with 15-23% upside from Thursday's closing of 235.8. CDMO revenue rose 36% year-on-year to 1,424 crore in the September quarter, supported by strong demand, better execution and higher capacity utilisation. The mix is also turning more favourable, with innovation-related work contributing 49% of CDMO revenue in the first half of FY27 compared with 46% a year ago while the share of differentiated offerings increased to 43% compared with 40% a year ago.

Strong growth in high value businesses such as on-patent manufacturing and antibody-drug conjugates (ADC), a targeted cancer therapy, should support margins in the coming quarters. A growing Phase III pipeline and 22 new customers added in the first half provide visibility on future CDMO growth. Investments in biologics and sterile fill-finish through the Yapan Bio acquisition and the Lexington facility expansion are strengthening Piramal Pharma's capabilities in complex manufacturing, including ADCs.

Beyond CDMO, Complex Hospital Generics is another growth driver, which delivered 32% revenue growth in the September quarter, led by strong ex-US inhalation anaesthesia sales and the ramp-up of the recently acquired Kenalog injectable portfolio. The consumer healthcare division grew 13% in the quarter, driven by power brands and e-commerce. The company stated that expiry of the low-margin Bayer distribution agreement may weigh on revenue but could improve consolidated Ebitda margin by around 50 bps.

Motilal Oswal Financial Services raised its FY27-FY28 earnings estimates by 7-11%, citing an improved CDMO demand outlook, scaling up of the ADC business, stronger supplier collaboration and portfolio enhancement in consumer healthcare segment. ICICI Securities raised its Ebitda estimates for the period by 1-6%, supported by strong customer enquiries and order inflows, new molecule additions and a growing commercial pipeline.

data.title: Japan Core Inflation Likely at 2.6% in November, Barclays Says — Market Talk
data.description: Japan's nationwide core consumer inflation, which excludes fresh food, likely accelerated to 2.6% on year in November from 2.2% in October, mirroring the pickup in Tokyo, Barclays economists estimate. They maintain their outlook for nationwide inflation to gradually rise going forward, citing renewed increases in oil procurement costs. However, the economists note that companies are passing less of their higher labor costs on to consumers than in 2024 and 2025, meaning recent wage growth momentum is unlikely to generate meaningful second-round inflationary effects. Government data earlier Friday showed Tokyo core consumer inflation picked up to 2.9% on year in November from October's 2.6% rise. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

data.title: Indonesia's plasma plant could cut drug prices 24.6%
data.description:
A blood plasma fractionation plant in Karawang, West Java, could make plasma-based medicines between 10.9% and 24.6% cheaper than imported equivalents, Kontan reports.

The figures come from a study by the Indonesia Investment Authority (INA), the country's sovereign wealth fund, and the Institute for Economic and Social Research (LPEM) at the University of Indonesia's Faculty of Economics and Business. The study looked at INA's investment in PT SKPlasma Core Indonesia, which will process donated blood plasma into medicines that Indonesia currently buys from abroad.

Lower prices would deliver affordability benefits worth IDR1.43 trillion (about $77.8mn) between 2024 and 2037, the study found.

Oki Ramadhana, chairman of INA's board of directors, said the plant would turn blood plasma into essential medicines at affordable prices with a secure supply. He said it would also help build the skills of the local workforce.

Speaking at the launch of INA's second socio-economic impact report in South Jakarta, Ramadhana said the facility was the first and largest plasma fractionation plant outside China, and that INA had built it with its partners.

The study estimates that the investment will add IDR26 trillion in value to gross domestic product. It puts the direct and indirect fiscal impact at IDR2.44 trillion.

The project is expected to support around 7,221 direct and indirect jobs each year.

In a separate investment in the sector, as Kontan reports, that Takeda plans to spend IDR539bn on a plasma bank in Indonesia, with technology transfer included.

data.title: Thailand's October exports rise 27.5% on year, highest in 5 years
data.description:
Thailand's customs-cleared exports (THCEX=ECI) rose 27.5% in October from a year earlier, the highest rate in five years, the commerce ministry said on Friday.

  • The October reading was above the forecast increase of 26.2% in a Reuters poll

  • Imports rose 53.2% in October from a year earlier, compared with the poll's forecast rise of 32.1%

  • Exports were seen rising more than 19% this year, Nantapong Chiralerspong, head of the ministry's Trade Policy and Strategy Office, told a media briefing

  • In the January-October period, exports increased 20.4% annually

  • October exports to the United States, Thailand's largest market, rose 42.9% from a year earlier, while shipments to China were up 21.3%, the ministry said

  • Thailand recorded a trade deficit (THCTR=ECI) of $12.34 billion in October, compared with a forecast deficit of $5.89 billion

data.title: Christopher Luxon favoured for second term as New Zealand Prime Minister
data.description:
Former businessman Christopher Luxon is in poll position for a second term as New Zealand's prime minister, overcoming falling personal popularity and two internal leadership challenges to keep the centre-right National Party in power.

Luxon, 56, entered parliament only in 2020 after a career in business, including as chief executive of Air New Zealand. He became National Party leader in late 2021 and led the party back to power in 2023, ending six years of Labour-led government.

His first term was marked by pressure over living costs, weak economic growth and tensions within the three-party governing coalition with the libertarian ACT New Zealand and populist New Zealand First.

Luxon also faced two public challenges to his leadership from within National over the past year, a rare occurrence in New Zealand politics, as opinion polls showed waning support for him personally. He survived both, arguing that his government needed to remain focused on reviving the economy, restraining spending and improving public services.

A former executive at global consumer goods group Unilever, Luxon has sought to apply a corporate management style to government, often talking of setting clear targets and holding ministers and public agencies accountable for delivery.

He has led efforts to curb government debt, reduce regulation and lift economic growth, presenting those policies as central to easing pressure on middle-income households.

Throughout negotiations "my focus will stay on what matters most to Kiwis, and that is growing the economy, easing the cost of living and continuing to fix the basics and build a future," Luxon said following the release of final results.

A millionaire father of two with several properties, Luxon has at times struggled to shake criticism that he is out of touch with ordinary voters. His public persona has also produced lighter moments: a Taylor Swift fan, he quoted the US pop star in televised debates and later invited her to marry in New Zealand during a pitch to promote the country internationally.

In a country where almost half the population identifies as having no religion, Luxon has faced scrutiny over his Christian faith and his personal opposition to abortion.

Luxon has also had to develop a higher international profile in office. He has backed Ukraine following Russia's invasion and broadly maintained New Zealand's traditional alignment with Western partners, while his government has taken a more outspoken stance on China's growing influence in the Pacific.

data.title: Dollar set for longest winning run since 2024 on AI risk
data.description:
The dollar is poised for its longest monthly winning streak in two years as a rupture in the artificial intelligence trade and rising interest rates spur demand for safe-haven assets.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index is up 1.9% in November, putting it on track for a third straight month of gains. The greenback has strengthened against all of its Group-of-10 peers, including the Japanese yen and the Swiss franc.

A slump in technology stocks, coupled with robust economic growth and elevated inflation, propelled the dollar higher over the past three months. The greenback held near its strongest level since April 2025 in early Asian trading after jumping in pre-holiday US hours on Wednesday, as the Nasdaq 100 index briefly plunged into a bear market and a measure of underlying inflation hit the highest since 2023.

“It’s a pretty good dollar storm,” said Steven Englander, co-head of FX research and North America macro strategy at Standard Chartered.

Market repricing for a more hawkish Federal Reserve also supported the dollar this month, according to Sarah Ying, CIBC’s head of FX strategy.

Traders are fully pricing a 25 basis point interest rate hike next month for the Fed, and are betting on the possibility of two additional increases by the middle of next year. Policymakers have been flagging the need for more tightening, with some calling for lifting rates at successive meetings, while others are open to the possibility of raising by more than the usual quarter percentage point in December.

Some Wall Street strategists expect the dollar rally to extend into 2027, pointing to the very AI spending binge that’s making stock markets jittery as a driver of US economic growth and capital flows. The greenback has benefited from overseas investors converting local currencies to buy shares of US companies that use the tech.

“The US economy is booming and inflation is still moving away from the target,” said Win Thin, chief economist at Bank of Nassau 1982. “The Fed needs to hike rates to help cool the economy, perhaps in both December and January. That’s dollar positive.”

The dollar’s latest surge has won over short-dated options traders, but conviction further out has weakened over the past two months. The divergence suggests investors are positioning for dollar strength into early 2027 while becoming less willing to extend bullish bets much further.

The latest equities sell-off has raised concerns about the longevity of the AI boom, fueling sharp swings in global markets. In such an environment, the dollar has become “the haven of choice,” according to Goldman Sachs, while MUFG believes that the prospect of higher rates is also helping the currency.

“Weakness in the US equity market is taking place at a time when there is building evidence of strengthening cyclical growth momentum in the US, which is encouraging a stronger US dollar as a safe haven play,” said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG.

“The strength of the US economy supports the view of investors that returns are likely to remain higher in the US even if they are currently being challenged by the recent sell-off in US assets,” he said.

data.title: Indian shares open flat after recent rally, set for fifth weekly gain
data.description:
Indian shares opened little changed on Friday, poised to post a fifth straight week of gains, with the unwinding of the global AI trade driving a return of foreign flows into local stocks.

The Nifty 50 slipped 0.04% to 25,869 while the Sensex eased 0.2% to 84,127.81, as of 9:18 a.m. IST.

Nine of the 16 major sectors logged gains. The broader small-caps and mid-caps gained 0.6% each.

The 50-stock Nifty index and the Sensex are up 0.3% each so far this week, consolidating after a blistering surge of 14.2% and 14.8%, respectively, over the last four weeks.

Brent crude futures hovered around $96 per barrel as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region.

data.title: Rocket Lab Launches 101st Electron Mission
data.description:
Key points:
  • Rocket Lab  launched another dedicated Electron mission for Japanese synthetic aperture radar satellite operator Synspective, deploying its 14th StriX satellite into low Earth orbit.
  • Dubbed “Night Owls Never Sleep,” the mission lifted off from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 1:15 p.m. NZDT on Sept. 27, 2026, delivering the satellite to a 569-kilometer orbit. The addition will expand Synspective’s Earth-observation constellation, which captures high-resolution images regardless of weather conditions or time of day.
  • The launch marked Rocket Lab’s 22nd mission of 2026 and its 101st overall, further extending Electron’s position as the world’s most frequently launched small-lift orbital rocket.
